summary: All notebook semantic and integration checks passed. The tutorial documents a single BADGE method run, and its live loop retrains, acquires, maps indices, and evaluates in the correct order.

checks_summary.note: The notebook evaluates predictions on the separate test set with the model's argmax and records the resulting accuracy curve; no training-label shortcut or constant predictor is used.
The BADGE sections describe hallucinated final-layer gradient embeddings, k-MEANS++ over those embeddings, and the same select_batch path used by the code.
The notebook's citations to Algorithm 1, Section 3, Equation 1, Proposition 1, and Appendix A Algorithm 2 match the corresponding paper-map locations.
Each acquisition round calls train_and_evaluate after updating the labeled set, and the curve records the returned test accuracy.
train_and_evaluate constructs a fresh model before every training call, including after each acquisition.
Returned positions are mapped through chosen_global = unlabeled_idx[selected_positions], followed by disjoint union/difference updates.
The initial set is evaluated once and range(cfg["num_rounds"]) performs one acquisition and post-acquisition evaluation per round, yielding num_rounds+1 points.
The notebook makes no independent ranking-score claim that conflicts with code; its k-MEANS++ prose correctly describes squared nearest-center distance sampling.

The live notebook calls BADGE select_batch on the unlabeled pool, whose reviewed path computes final-layer gradient embeddings and then k-MEANS++ seeding; no baseline or forbidden substitution is introduced.

caveats: The notebook intentionally uses smoke-scale defaults, one seed, five rounds, and a flattened MLP rather than the paper's full SVHN benchmark protocol; these departures are explicitly disclosed in the opening and parameter sections.
